hints: Focus on the two clues together, the starting Mr must be 84 and it must be able to add HBr.
Calculate Mr for each skeleton, remember $C=12$, $H=1$, $O=16$, so $C_6H_{12}$ gives $72+12=84$.
Check what $84 + 80.9$ gives and ask which functional group adds a whole molecule of HBr across a double bond.
walkthrough:
**Work out what Mr = 84 means**

Think of the common building blocks. A hydrocarbon with formula $C_6H_{12}$ has Mr exactly 84.

$$M_r = (6 \times 12) + (12 \times 1) = 72 + 12 = 84$$

**Work out what the HBr product tells us**

$HBr$ has Mr about 80.9 ($1 + 79.9$). Addition of one $HBr$ gives:

$$84 + 80.9 = 164.9$$
This is exactly electrophilic addition across a $C=C$ double bond to give a bromoalkane, $C_6H_{12} + HBr \rightarrow C_6H_{13}Br$.

**Test the four structures**

A is cyclohexane, $C_6H_{12}$, Mr = 84 but it is a cycloalkane with no $C=C$, so no addition of HBr.
C is pentan-3-one, $CH_3CH_2COCH_2CH_3$, $C_5H_{10}O$, Mr = 86, and ketones do not add HBr in this way.
B is a longer alkene, a $C_7$ alkene ($C_7H_{14}$, Mr = 98), so it fails the first test.
D is hex-3-ene, $CH_3CH_2CH=CHCH_2CH_3$, $C_6H_{12}$, Mr = 84 and it has a $C=C$ to add HBr to give Mr 164.9.

options.A: Cyclohexane is $C_6H_{12}$ so Mr is 84, which fits the first clue. However it is saturated with only single bonds, so it does not undergo electrophilic addition with HBr to give a product of Mr 164.9.
options.B: This is a $C_7$ alkene (heptene, $C_7H_{14}$). It would add HBr, but its starting Mr is $(7 \times 12)+14 = 98$, not 84, so it fails the first condition.
options.C: Pentan-3-one is $C_5H_{10}O$. Its Mr is $(5 \times 12)+10+16 = 86$, not 84. The $C=O$ group also does not add HBr to give a bromoalkane of Mr 164.9.
options.D: Hex-3-ene is $C_6H_{12}$, so Mr = 84. As an alkene it undergoes addition with HBr: $C_6H_{12} + HBr \rightarrow C_6H_{13}Br$ with Mr = $84 + 80.9 = 164.9$. Both conditions are met.
